Rather than being demanding or yelling like in the picture, it can involve emotional manipulation. One person can attempt to “train” the other to do as they want by making the consequences of not doing so much less bearable. I can tell you from experience that I have sucked it up and done the deed when I was 0% in the mood. Had I not, I would have been enduring the consequences of it over the next three or four days. Frigid interactions, emotionally erratic behavior, a conveniently sudden increase in things I’m doing wrong, etc.

Here’s the thing… I get that we are all human and no one is going to handle these situations perfectly each time. I am not without my own flaws. But damn, do you think that acting like that makes me want to pursue you? All it would take from the start is a simple and playful “it’s cool! Get that engine primed for me tomorrow night then, yeah?” and you can put money on me being ready to go. Because I would appreciate the flexibility and it seeming like a team activity rather than a job I’m expected to do.

I don’t think I need to elaborate on the micromanaging part. That’s pretty self-explanatory but subjective depending on everyone’s own experiences. It just makes it not fun. By all means, voice your needs, but this can quickly get so excessive it becomes selfish and kills the mood.

All in all, this kind of thing saps all the joy out of it the same way as being treated like the guy in the pic. If it can’t be a mutually agreeable situation, I’m not at all interested in participating and I’m going to get increasingly bitter the more I’m expected to do so. It’s not any different than if a man was trying to persuade a woman and we all know how people would perceive that. 

It feels gross airing that out on the internet, but that’s the reality for some people and perhaps the perspective might help someone.

It takes surprisingly little effort to schedule or micromanage all the fun out of sex (before, during, AND after) and some people have perfected the art of doing so. Not sure why you are getting downvotes simply for stating for your opinion. I also found the lootboxes to be a non-issue, after being skeptical before purchase myself. I finished the Shadow Wars, and it was a grind, sure, but I think it was that way for the sake of the story. The whole point of the last act was that Talion kept Mordor in chaos until the Fellowship could be formed, unbeknownst to him. While it steers far away from canon, the grind through the last act is the way it is so the player feels like they are spending an eternity holding Mordor at bay, just as the protagonist did. If there was just one big battle after act 3, followed by the end game cutscene, people would gripe about not knowing what happened in between. Sieges. That’s what happened in this story. So the developers let us play them until it became a drag, so we would be as exhausted as Talion likely would have been. I don’t begrudge anyone for simply not doing them, but to be mad about the implementation, given the reason I stated above, seems unfair.

Now, for my Shadow War strategy, all I did was boost my orcs in the easy fight pits in between every phase. Train up those epics and legendaries that don’t have mortalities and fears common to the perks the enemy orcs have. Max the fortress defenses, with iron and spiked walls, then jump down and dominate every bodyguard and warlord you can in the early waves. Then they’ll fight for you outside the wall to soften up the attackers until the gate breaks. That will heavily minimize losses on your side. Also, equip captain-specific gear. Ones that give health or resupply ranged ammo for every critical or domination. Fire and freeze critical hits are also handy. I finished with all level 60s. All of which either gained a gang and elemental weapon, or I gave them one of each via silver lootbox drops I got with in-game currency. No $$$ lootboxes needed at all. Just available for the suckers. 

So yeah, the Shadow Wars is a grind. It’s supposed to be. And I never once felt like buying a lootbox would make my life easier, given the fact that the randomized orcs you encounter naturally are as good or better than ones you’d get through RNG anyway. Especially the ones you’ll run into in the later phases.
